name: MCP Upgrades: LXC, Static Sites & Routing
description: Design spec and machine-readable MCP tool definitions that bring ProxyPilot's LXC, static-site, and edge-routing management to parity with its projects tooling. Derived from a real deployment session: six bugfixes for the existing surface (empty list_lxc_containers, broken list_static_sites, missing timeouts, silent zip corruption), plus 25 new tool definitions across five domains — read-only LXC observability, allowlisted in-guest exec, gated lifecycle/config with snapshot-before-mutate, route inspection/testing/binding, and static-site file management. Deliberately contains no delete verbs and no arbitrary shell.
usage_md:
# Integrating the MCP upgrade spec

This component is a **design spec + machine-readable tool definitions**, not
runtime code. It targets the ProxyPilot admin backend — the codebase that
implements the existing MCP tools (`list_lxc_containers`, `read_lxc_file`,
`apply_lxc_zip`, `run_project_command`, …). Import it into that project so a
build cycle can implement the tools against the definitions here.

## 1. Dependencies

None to install. Every file is JSON or Markdown consumed at build/design time.
Implementation work will use whatever the host project already uses for its MCP
server and Incus access (no new runtime deps are prescribed by this spec).

## 2. Wiring / how to consume

- `docs/00-overview.md` — read first: rationale, non-destructive design
  principles, and priority order. The priority order is the intended build
  order; item 1 (bugfixes) blocks everything else.
- `docs/01-bugfixes.md` — six defects in the *existing* tool surface, each with
  observed behavior, likely cause, and an acceptance criterion. Fix these before
  adding new tools; agents make decisions on the output of the broken ones.
- `schemas/*.tools.json` — MCP tool definitions in the standard shape
  (`name`, `description`, `inputSchema` as JSON Schema). Register each tool on
  the MCP server the same way the existing tools are registered; the
  `description` strings are written to be served verbatim to MCP clients.
  Example registration sketch (adapt to the host project's server API):

  ```js
  const observe = require('./spec/mcp-upgrades/schemas/lxc-observe.tools.json');
  for (const t of observe.tools) {
    server.registerTool(t.name, t.description, t.inputSchema, handlers[t.name]);
  }
  ```

- `policy/lxc-command-allowlist.json` — load at server start; `run_lxc_command`
  must validate argv against `read_only` + `mutating_scoped` and reject anything
  matching `deny_always` or containing `shell_syntax_rejected` tokens.
  `deny_always` wins over any allow rule. `mutating_scoped` commands are legal
  only when `working_dir` equals the guest's registered startup working dir.
- `policy/lxc-config-allowlist.json` — the only keys `set_lxc_config` may write,
  with the gate each requires. `explicitly_not_writable` documents keys that
  must stay rejected and why — keep that reasoning in code comments.

## 3. Configuration

No new env vars are required by the spec itself. Implementations will need
whatever Incus socket/remote credentials the existing LXC tools already use.
Two constants in `policy/lxc-command-allowlist.json` are tunable:
`output_cap_bytes` (default 65536, matching `run_project_command`) and
`default_timeout_seconds` / `max_timeout_seconds` (120 / 1800).

## 4. Layout

- `docs/` — human-readable spec (overview + bugfixes). Not served to clients.
- `schemas/` — one `*.tools.json` per domain: `lxc-observe` (6 read-only tools),
  `lxc-exec` (constrained exec, 2 tools), `lxc-lifecycle` (7 tools, all gated),
  `routing` (4 tools), `static-sites` (6 tools). Descriptions inside the schema
  files and the two policy files must be kept in sync — the policy files are the
  enforcement source of truth; the descriptions summarize them.
- `policy/` — enforcement data loaded at runtime by the exec and config tools.
- No tests are included; acceptance criteria live in `docs/01-bugfixes.md` and
  in each tool description.

## 5. Security caveats

- **No delete verbs, by design.** Do not "complete" the surface with
  `delete_lxc_container` / `delete_static_site` / arbitrary shell — their absence
  is the spec's central safety property, not an omission.
- **`security.privileged` is the sharpest edge.** The tool must require
  `acknowledge_risk: true`, surface the warning text from
  `policy/lxc-config-allowlist.json` in its result, and snapshot first.
  Container root becomes host root; the warning exists because a real operator
  chose this path in the field after being steered away.
- **Snapshot-before-mutate is load-bearing.** Every mutating tool assumes
  `snapshot_lxc_container` ran first; implement it before any of them.
- **The exec allowlist is prefix-matched argv, never a shell.** If the
  implementation ever passes the command line to `sh -c`, the entire allowlist
  is void. `curl` is probe-only: its output-writing flags are in `deny_always`.
- **`probe_lxc_port` / `test_route` must never return response bodies** — only
  status metadata. Bodies can contain credentials echoed by misconfigured apps.
- **Upload checksum (bugfix #4) closes a silent-corruption path** that today
  surfaces as a confusing extraction error; implement it in the inspect step,
  before any bytes touch a guest.

files.content:
# ProxyPilot MCP Upgrades — LXC, Static Sites, Routing

Design spec for bringing ProxyPilot's LXC container, static-site, and edge-routing
management up to parity with its AI-dev **projects** tooling, over MCP.

## Why this exists (field evidence)

This spec was derived from a real deployment session (2026-08-12): installing a
`linuxserver/chrome` Docker container inside the `Web` LXC guest and routing
`web.fractionate.ai` to it. A straightforward install took five redeploy cycles
because the MCP surface has **deploy verbs but almost no observe verbs**:

- `list_lxc_containers` returned `[]` while the `Web` container was live and
  reachable by name — the operator was told to create a container that existed.
- `list_static_sites` threw `no such column: domain` — static-site management is
  unreachable over MCP entirely.
- There was no way to learn a guest's IP, privilege mode, or listening ports
  without **editing the registered boot script and redeploying** to smuggle
  `ip addr` / `ss` / `curl` output through startup stdout.
- The edge 502 (proxy → stale upstream) was invisible: no route inspection, no
  route test, no way to distinguish "proxy misconfigured" from "app down".
- A privileged-mode flip and container restart had to be done by hand on the
  Incus host (`incus config set pp-Web security.privileged=true`) because no
  config or lifecycle tool exists.
- Inline base64 zip upload corrupted silently (`declared 3472, got 3460`); the
  upload-ticket path was unreachable from the sandboxed agent's network.

## Design principles (non-destructive by construction)

1. **Observe first.** The bulk of new tools are read-only and carry zero risk.
2. **No delete verbs.** No `delete_lxc_container`, no `delete_static_site`, no
   arbitrary shell. Removal stays a human/host operation.
3. **Confirm + snapshot on every mutation.** Mutating tools require
   `confirm: true` and take an automatic snapshot (or `.old` backup) first,
   extending the pattern `write_lxc_file` already uses.
4. **Allowlists, not shells.** `run_lxc_command` mirrors `run_project_command`:
   whitespace-split argv, no shell metacharacters, read-biased command allowlist
   (see `policy/lxc-command-allowlist.json`).
5. **Config keys are gated.** `set_lxc_config` only accepts an allowlisted key
   set; `security.privileged` additionally requires `acknowledge_risk: true`.
6. **Parity with projects.** Every proposal maps to an existing projects-side
   tool (`list_project_files`, `search_project_files`, `run_project_command`,
   `project_git_diff`, `get_project`) — same ergonomics, same safety posture.

## Package layout

- `docs/01-bugfixes.md` — defects to fix before any new surface is added.
- `schemas/*.tools.json` — MCP tool definitions (name, description, JSON Schema
  input), grouped by domain, ready to register on the ProxyPilot MCP server.
- `policy/lxc-command-allowlist.json` — the exec allowlist for `run_lxc_command`.
- `policy/lxc-config-allowlist.json` — writable Incus config keys and their gates.

## Priority order

1. **Bugfixes** (docs/01) — they block everything else.
2. `run_lxc_command` + `get_lxc_container` — would have collapsed the field
   session from five redeploys to two calls.
3. Routing tools (`get_route` / `test_route` / `set_route`) — the actual failure
   layer in the field session.
4. LXC lifecycle/config (create, start/stop/restart, set_config, snapshot,
   set_network).
5. Static-site parity.
6. Cross-cutting upload/checksum/mode fixes.

# Bugfixes required before new surface

These are defects in the existing MCP tools, observed in the field on
2026-08-12. They should land before (or with) the first new tool, because
agents make *decisions* on their output.

## 1. `list_lxc_containers` returns `[]` for live containers

**Observed:** returned `{"containers": []}` while the Incus guest `pp-Web` was
running and every name-addressed tool (`read_lxc_file`, `write_lxc_file`,
`apply_lxc_zip`, `rerun_startup`) operated on `Web` successfully.

**Impact:** highest of any issue. An agent (or human) concludes no containers
exist and plans creation of a duplicate. Discovery-by-probing (calling
`read_lxc_file` against guessed names, distinguishing "Instance not found" from
"Not a file") is the only workaround.

**Likely cause:** the list endpoint reads a registry table that containers are
never written to (registration only happens through some other path), or it
queries the wrong Incus project/remote. Note the error text on misses —
`Failed to fetch instance "pp-web" in project "default"` — shows the tool layer
lowercases and prefixes names (`Web` → `pp-web` vs the real `pp-Web`); check the
list path for the same normalization bug.

**Fix acceptance:** every guest the file tools can reach by name appears in the
list with `name`, `status`, and `ip`.

## 2. `list_static_sites` throws `no such column: domain`

**Observed:** hard SQL error on every call. The MCP description promises
`(id, name, domain)`.

**Impact:** the static-sites domain is entirely unmanageable over MCP — the
deploy tools (`inspect_static_site_zip` / `apply_static_site_zip`) need an id
that can only come from this broken call.

**Likely cause:** schema drift — a migration renamed/moved the `domain` column
(e.g. to a `routes` table) and the tool's SELECT was never updated.

**Fix acceptance:** returns the site list; `domain` populated from wherever the
routing data actually lives now.

## 3. `rerun_startup` lacks `timeout_seconds` and any output ceiling

**Observed:** a first-boot run performed a full Docker engine install plus a
910 MB image pull inside one blocking call, with no timeout parameter (unlike
`run_project_command`, which has `timeout_seconds` up to 1800 and a 64 KB output
cap) and no way to cancel.

**Fix acceptance:** `rerun_startup` accepts `timeout_seconds` (same semantics as
`run_project_command`, including `timed_out: true` in the result) and truncates
stdout/stderr to the last 64 KB.

## 4. Inline zip upload corrupts silently

**Observed:** `apply_lxc_zip` failed with `Zip entry size mismatch (declared
3472, got 3460)` on a well-formed archive delivered via `zip_base64`. Nothing in
the transport reported corruption; it surfaced only at extraction.

**Fix:** accept an optional `sha256` field alongside `zip_base64` / `ticket` in
the inspect tools; verify before extraction and fail with a transport-corruption
error rather than an extraction error.

## 5. Upload tickets are unreachable from sandboxed agents

**Observed:** `create_upload_ticket` returns a PUT URL on
`edge.fractionate.ai`, which egress-restricted agent sandboxes cannot reach
(CONNECT 403). So the documented path for zips over ~2 MB is closed to exactly
the clients most likely to be driving these tools.

**Fix:** add a chunked-append fallback over MCP itself — e.g.
`append_upload_chunk(ticket, seq, chunk_base64)` + `finish_upload(ticket,
sha256)` — so large archives can be delivered through the already-working MCP
channel.

## 6. `write_lxc_file` cannot set the execute bit

**Observed:** a script written via `write_lxc_file` is not runnable; the only
way to deliver an executable file is a zip apply.

**Fix:** optional `mode` parameter (octal string, e.g. `"0755"`), defaulting to
current behavior.

  "$comment": "Allowlist for run_lxc_command. Matching is on argv prefix after whitespace-split; no shell is ever invoked, so metacharacters are inert but rejected anyway for clarity. deny_always wins over any allow rule.",
  "read_only": [
    ["docker", "ps"],
    ["docker", "inspect"],
    ["docker", "logs"],
    ["docker", "images"],
    ["docker", "compose", "ps"],
    ["docker", "compose", "logs"],
    ["docker", "compose", "config"],
    ["systemctl", "status"],
    ["systemctl", "is-active"],
    ["systemctl", "is-enabled"],
    ["journalctl"],
    ["ip", "addr"],
    ["ip", "-4", "addr"],
    ["ip", "route"],
    ["ip", "-4", "route"],
    ["ss"],
    ["sysctl", "-n"],
    ["curl"],
    ["df"],
    ["free"],
    ["uname"],
    ["cat", "/etc/os-release"],
    ["ls"],
    ["stat"],
    ["du"]
  ],
  "mutating_scoped": {
    "$comment": "Allowed only with working_dir equal to the registered startup working dir, so an agent can manage the app it deployed but nothing else.",
    "commands": [
      ["docker", "compose", "up", "-d"],
      ["docker", "compose", "restart"],
      ["docker", "compose", "stop"],
      ["docker", "compose", "pull"],
      ["docker", "restart"],
      ["systemctl", "restart", "docker"]
    ]
  },
  "deny_always": {
    "$comment": "Never allowed regardless of other rules.",
    "commands": [
      ["rm"], ["rmdir"], ["mv"], ["dd"], ["mkfs"],
      ["shutdown"], ["reboot"], ["halt"], ["poweroff"],
      ["docker", "compose", "down"],
      ["docker", "rm"], ["docker", "rmi"], ["docker", "system", "prune"], ["docker", "volume", "rm"],
      ["apt"], ["apt-get"], ["dpkg"],
      ["useradd"], ["userdel"], ["passwd"], ["chpasswd"],
      ["iptables"], ["nft"],
      ["sh"], ["bash"], ["dash"], ["zsh"], ["python"], ["python3"], ["perl"], ["node"],
      ["chmod"], ["chown"],
      ["ssh"], ["scp"], ["nc"], ["ncat"], ["socat"],
      ["curl", "-o"], ["curl", "--output"], ["curl", "-O"], ["wget"]
    ],
    "rationale": {
      "docker compose down": "Removes containers and networks; restart/stop cover every legitimate need without deletion.",
      "apt/apt-get/dpkg": "Package changes belong in the startup script where they are recorded and re-runnable, not in ad-hoc exec.",
      "shells and interpreters": "Would make the allowlist a formality.",
      "curl with output flags / wget": "curl is allowed for probing only; writing fetched bytes to disk is arbitrary code delivery."
    }
  },
  "shell_syntax_rejected": ["|", ">", ">>", "<", ";", "&&", "||", "$(", "`", "&"],
  "output_cap_bytes": 65536,
  "default_timeout_seconds": 120,
  "max_timeout_seconds": 1800
}
